title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 12
statement: Al, Betty, and Clare split \(\$1000\) among them to be invested in different ways. Each begins with a different amount. At the end of one year they have a total of \(\$1500.\) Betty and Clare have both doubled their money, whereas Al has managed to lose \(\$100.\) What was Al’s original portion?

solutions.text:
Let \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) be the original portions. Then \(a+b+c=1000\) and \((a-100)+2(b+c)=1500.\)

Substituting \(b+c=1000-a\) into the second equation, \[a-100+2(1000-a)=1500,\] so \(a=400.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let Al, Betty, and Clare start with \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c,\) so \(a+b+c=1000\)
